newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan BSPA passes on tender for 54,000T soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan BSPA passes on tender for 54,000T soybeans.

text.p: The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association passed on a tender on Friday for a 54,000-tonne shipment of Argentine or Brazilian soybeans, due to the government's ban on prok export, traders said.
Traders said a pork export ban has disrupted Taiwan's demand for soymeal, a byproduct in soybean crushing, so buyers passed on Friday's tenders to review schedule of their shipments.
Traders said Taiwan's overall demand for soybean would decline slightly.
"Soybean imports will drop a little, as soymeal demand is expected to fall," a soybean buyer said.
Earlier on Friday Taiwan Sugar Corp cancelled a Friday's tender for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans.
Another Taiwan corn buying group Members Feed Industry Group passed on a tender for up to 112,000 tonnes corn also due to the ban.

Taiwan's cabinet-level Council of Agriculture on Thursday banned all exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of the deadly and highly contagious foot and mouth disease in the island's hog population.
Japan's Agriculture Ministry on Friday banned Taiwan's pork imports indefinitely in the wake of the outbreak.
South Korea also announced a similar ban.
Traders said they expected the BSPA's Taichung division to return to the market to tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment at a later date.
"The BSPA group is likely to tender for a similar size shipment with later shipping date," a trader said.
The breakfast association's Taichung division consists of Sino Japan Feed Corp, Chia Hsin, Formosa Oilseed, Fwu Sow Grain, and Tay Shan.
